<h1>Mohammad Rafiqul Islam</h1>
<div class="role"><b>Postdoctoral Research Associate</b> · Iowa State University </div>

<p class="lede">I design and analyze Langevin algorithms: Markov chain Monte Carlo methods for sampling high-dimensional distributions across networks of agents, inside constrained domains, and at higher orders of accuracy. At Iowa State I work with David&nbsp;P.&nbsp;Herzog. I earned my Ph.D. at Florida State University in 2026, advised by Lingjiong&nbsp;Zhu.</p>

<h2>Research Spotlight</h2>
<a class="text-link" href="research.qmd">All research</a>
:::

::: {.theme-grid}
::: {.theme-card}
<div class="num"><span>I.</span><span class="status">current · 2026</span></div>
<h3>Constrained dynamics with singular repulsion</h3>
<p>Collision-free stochastic particle systems inside a constrained domain, and numerical schemes that stay stable near the singularity without creating artificial collisions. Joint work with D.&nbsp;P.&nbsp;Herzog.</p>
<div class="refs"><a href="research/singular-langevin/" target="_blank">Project overview</a></div>
:::

::: {.theme-card}
<div class="num"><span>II.</span><span class="status">2024 – 2026</span></div>
<h3>Decentralized Bayesian sampling</h3>
<p>Agents on a network sample a shared posterior without pooling their data. This line of work removes network bias with EXTRA-type corrections and handles convex constraints through proximal regularization.</p>
<div class="refs"><a href="research/extrasgld/" target="_blank">Generalized EXTRA SGLD</a><a href="research/dpsgld/" target="_blank">Decentralized Proximal SGLD</a></div>
:::

::: {.theme-card}
<div class="num"><span>III.</span><span class="status">2025</span></div>
<h3>High-order Langevin Monte Carlo</h3>
<p>Samplers built from $P$-th order Langevin dynamics through splitting and accurate integration. Their Wasserstein guarantees depend better on the dimension and the accuracy level as the order grows.</p>
<div class="refs"><a href="research/holmc/" target="_blank">High-Order Langevin Monte Carlo</a></div>
:::
:::
